text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The National Bank of Slovakia (NSB) said it was not considering an imminent devaluation of the crown.
- The NBS said it had expected the trade deficit in its monetary programme for this year, but admitted the growth of the deficit had been faster than expected.
- Slovak hard currency reserves are sufficient to allow the NBS to maintain the current fixing regime of the Slovak crown, the central bank said.
- Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma begins a state visit to Slovakia on Wednesday.

- Economics Minister Karol Cesnek said Slovakia was preparing measures to boost its trade with Russia. The measures include creation of a special pro-export fund, and a special bank providing loans to Slovak companies exporting to Russia.

- Slovakia's largest drug producer Slovakofarma has issued 350 million crowns worth of five-year bonds, with a fixed coupon rate at 11.6 percent. The company plans to issue another 150 million in similar bonds by the end of this year.

- President Michal Kovac refused to sign the recently approved law according to which the second channel of the official Slovak Television (STV2) should broadcast via satelite and the channel's terrestrial network should be operated by a private company. Kovac returned the law to the parliament for revision.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Annual tax evasion caused by the shadow economy is estimated at seven to 10 billion crowns in direct taxes, and five to 10 billion crowns in indirect taxes.

- Slovakia's sole producer of lighting equipment, Osram Slovakia a.s., said it planned to double its annual turnover to around 700 million crowns next year. Exports are expected to account for 75 percent of overall production.

SME - The overall tax burden on Slovak citizens amounted to 44.4 percent last year, compared with an average tax burden of 40.5 percent in the European Union. The Finance Ministry said neither tax cuts nor tax hikes were planned.
